xs-itemize(5) ​

Itemize & out-format

Decode every character of an -i change line and every --out-format escape.

SYNOPSIS ​

sh
xs -ai SRC/ DEST/                 # one line per changed entry
xs -aii SRC/ DEST/                # also unchanged entries
xs -a --out-format='%i %n%L' SRC/ DEST/

-i prints one line for each entry the transfer changes. The line starts with an eleven-character change code, followed by the name. The code uses rsync’s layout, YXcstpoguax, so scripts written for rsync read it the same way. With --fileflags the code has a twelfth character. Every example below is real output from the current binary.

THE CHANGE CODE ​

PositionValuesMeaning
1 · Y< > c h . *What happened. < file data sent to the remote side (push); > file data received (local copy or pull); c a directory, symlink, device or special file was created or changed; h a hard link to another entry in the transfer (-H); . no data was transferred, so only attributes changed, or nothing did (-ii); * the rest of the line is a message, such as *deleting.
2 · Xf d L D SEntry type: regular file, directory, symlink, device, or special file (FIFO or socket).
3 · ccA regular file’s checksum differs (only computed with -c), or a symlink’s target changed.
4 · ssSize differs.
5 · tt TModification time differs. T means the time is being set to the transfer time because times are not preserved (no -t).
6 · ppPermissions differ.
7 · ooOwner differs.
8 · ggGroup differs.
9 · uu n bAccess time (u, with -U), creation time (n, with -N on macOS), or both (b) differ.
10 · aaACL differs (-A).
11 · xxExtended attributes differ (-X).
12 · ffBSD file flags differ. Present only with --fileflags, which is macOS only.

In positions 3 onward, . means “unchanged”. A new entry shows + in every attribute position, and -ii shows unchanged entries with spaces. Positions for attributes the transfer does not compare, such as ACLs without -A, stay ..

NEW ENTRIES ​

Itemize a fresh copy
sh
xs -ai src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
cd+++++++++ ./
cd+++++++++ archive/
>f+++++++++ archive/2026-q3.log
cd+++++++++ docs/
>f+++++++++ docs/guide.md
cd+++++++++ docs/images/
>f+++++++++ docs/images/diagram.svg
cL+++++++++ latest -> notes.txt
>f+++++++++ notes.txt
cd+++++++++ scripts/
>f+++++++++ scripts/build.sh

Directories end with /, and the destination root itself is ./. A symlink shows its target after -> .

CHANGES ​

The following run starts from a synced copy, then changes one attribute of each entry: content and group, time, mode, owner, access time, ACL, an extended attribute and a symlink target. It also adds a page, a device and a FIFO, and leaves a stale file in the destination.

Itemize every kind of change: content, time, mode, owner, group, access time, ACL, xattr, symlink target, new device and FIFO, deletion
sh
xs -aiXAUD --delete src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
.f....o.u.. archive/2026-q3.log
.d..t...... docs/
>f+++++++++ docs/faq.md
>f..t...u.. docs/guide.md
.d........x docs/images/
.f......ua. docs/images/diagram.svg
cLc........ latest -> docs/guide.md
>f.s...g... notes.txt
cD+++++++++ null
cS+++++++++ queue
.f...p..u.. scripts/build.sh
*deleting   stale.txt

Read .f....o.u.. archive/2026-q3.log as: no data sent (.), a regular file (f), owner changed (o), access time changed (u). Only the attributes were updated.

Same size and time, different content: only -c notices
sh
xs -aci src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
.f..t...... docs/guide.md
>fc........ notes.txt

Without -c, a file whose size and time match is skipped, so the content change to notes.txt would go unnoticed.

Without -t, updated files get the transfer time (T)
sh
xs -rli src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
>f.sT...... notes.txt

HARD LINKS ​

Hard-link groups with -H
sh
xs -aiH src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
cd+++++++++ ./
cd+++++++++ archive/
>f+++++++++ archive/2026-q3.log
cd+++++++++ docs/
>f+++++++++ docs/guide.md
cd+++++++++ docs/images/
>f+++++++++ docs/images/diagram.svg
>f+++++++++ docs/notes-link.txt
cL+++++++++ docs/readme-link.md -> guide.md
hL+++++++++ docs/readme.md => docs/readme-link.md
cL+++++++++ latest -> notes.txt
hf+++++++++ notes.txt => docs/notes-link.txt
cd+++++++++ scripts/
>f+++++++++ scripts/build.sh

With -H, the first member of a hard-link group is copied, and later members are reported as h lines that name the copied member after => . That is distinct from a symlink’s -> : hL is a symlink that is hard-linked to another symlink.

UNCHANGED ENTRIES ​

Repeat -i to list unchanged entries too
sh
xs -aii src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
.d          ./
.d          archive/
.f          archive/2026-q3.log
.d          docs/
.f          docs/guide.md
.d          docs/images/
.f          docs/images/diagram.svg
.L          latest -> notes.txt
.f          notes.txt
.d          scripts/
.f          scripts/build.sh

--OUT-FORMAT ​

EscapeExpands to
%iThe change code described above.
%nThe transfer-relative name, with a trailing / for directories.
%L -> TARGET for a symlink, => NAME for a hard link, otherwise empty.
%lThe source length in bytes.
%oThe operation: send, recv or del.
%fThe long source name on a sender, or the short name on a remote pull.
%bFile-content bytes transferred before compression, excluding framing. A resumed file counts only the tail that was sent; clones, metadata-only updates and dry runs count zero.
%tThe local date and time.
%%A literal %.

An optional width pads with spaces: %-24n left-aligns the name in 24 columns, and %10l right-aligns the length in 10.

Choose the fields of each file line
sh
xs -a --out-format='%o %i %-24n %10l %b' src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
send cd+++++++++ ./                             4096 0
send cd+++++++++ archive/                       4096 0
send >f+++++++++ archive/2026-q3.log         1288895 1288895
send cd+++++++++ docs/                          4096 0
send >f+++++++++ docs/guide.md                    33 33
send cd+++++++++ docs/images/                   4096 0
send >f+++++++++ docs/images/diagram.svg          42 42
send cL+++++++++ latest                            9 0
send >f+++++++++ notes.txt                        14 14
send cd+++++++++ scripts/                       4096 0
send >f+++++++++ scripts/build.sh                 21 21
DIFFERS FROM RSYNC

rsync’s %b counts protocol bytes, so it depends on rsync’s own framing and compression. xs counts file content. An empty --out-format='' suppresses file lines entirely.

ORDER, LOGS AND ESCAPING ​

  • Order. On a terminal, lines appear as each entry finishes. When stdout is a pipe or file, they are buffered until the end and sorted by path, so the output of a parallel transfer is still stable from run to run.
  • Logs. --log-file=FILE appends exactly the stdout stream, with no timestamps or prefixes added. -q suppresses the stream.
  • Escaping. Control bytes other than tab are written as \#ooo (octal). Valid UTF-8 is kept. Invalid high bytes are escaped unless -8/--8-bit-output is given.
  • Remote transfers. --out-format, --log-file and -ii need a helper that supports structured output; plain -v and -i work with older helpers. See protocol features.
